text_representation.reasoning: Embeds claim_norm only, not evidence_norm. Novelty of the INPUT CLAIM is what matters for routing decisions. The evidence_norm field in this restored dataset is retrieval-backfilled for many rows (see hackathon/restore_claim_training_fast.py), so including it would partly measure retrieval-corpus coverage rather than genuine claim novelty.

distance_metric_note: mean cosine distance (1 - cosine_similarity) to the k nearest neighbors in the TRAIN reference embedding set. Embeddings are L2-normalized by SentenceTransformer.encode(normalize_embeddings=True), so this is a monotonic transform of Euclidean distance on normalized vectors; cosine was used directly since it is sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors' native metric name for it.

thresholds.derivation: Computed from percentiles of the UNSUPERVISED novelty_score distribution over the VALIDATION split only (task_label was never consulted). score < lower_value -> FAMILIAR; lower_value <= score < upper_value -> MODERATELY NOVEL; score >= upper_value -> HIGHLY NOVEL.

warning: novelty_score / novelty_category are OOD/unfamiliarity signals, NOT misinformation scores. HIGHLY NOVEL does not mean 'Fake'; FAMILIAR does not mean 'Real'. task_label was never used to fit the reference distribution or the thresholds.
